question: Within detected migration initiators, does the same project-held-out activation-trained body-condition score rank whose detected migration onset occurs sooner after release?
source: Pinned same six-project stage-coded eel panel, 575 tracks, canonical nine expert-classified nonmigrants excluded from initiators.
scoring: Train stage+length+release and expanded stage+length+release+condition activation models on the other five projects, freeze all coefficients, score focal project; no focal outcome used in fitted weights.
target: Among eels with canonical initiated=TRUE and a nonnegative onset-release interval, continuous latency in days to source downstream movement onset.
primary: Within project-year, pairwise time-order concordance: if eel A begins sooner than B, did the frozen score of A exceed B? Report base and expanded C and their difference, with release-day ties omitted.
secondary: Sensitivity excluding onset within first 24 hours of release
Median and interquartile latency by Durif stage and project
Equal-project mean and six-project cluster-bootstrap CI on the base/expanded concordance difference
Project sign-flip descriptive exact p (2^n) for improvement
status_rule: Do not interpret a near 0.5 C-index as exact zero; interpret a general positive condition contribution only if project-resampled 95% CI for the additional concordance excludes zero and project signs do not strongly conflict.
boundaries: This conditions on having entered the source classified migration state, a phenotype-selected cohort; not a causal state effect on timing.
Source timestamps and receiver geometry may differ among rivers; interval from release is not a physiological initiation time.
Onset occurring on tagging/release day may be mechanically coupled to release, so explicitly show >1-day sensitivity.
Only six projects and pairwise observations share eels; infer using projects, not fish pairs.
This endpoint is not swimming velocity, passage success, escapement or mortality.
Do not equate failure to predict latency with no internal role in temporal gating under unobserved hydraulic/thermal cues.
